profile.name: Abdulrahman Bahjat
profile.title: Mechanical Engineering Student · Penn State
profile.intro: I'm a mechanical engineering student at Penn State who likes finishing what I start: prototypes and robots on one side, and on the other, apps people actually use, which I build by directing AI coding agents. This portfolio is a small star system, and each planet is a project.
bio: In engineering, I design things that have to hold up in real life. My folding cardboard chair held the weight of four people and was the best-performing design in my engineering design class, and in high school I designed and built my robotics team's VEX robot.

In software, my strongest tool is AI. I write the requirements, direct AI coding agents, test what they produce and drive every bug to a fix until the thing works. That is how I built an online store for a local chocolatier, MyRoom, MyKitchen, PrayerLock, and this site.

details: Coursework: Engineering Design, Statics, Dynamics, Mechanics, Matrices, Differential Equations, Programming for Engineers (MATLAB), Electricity & Magnetism

goals: Long term: space systems and robotics.
profile.availability: Open to internships and project collaborations.

projects.title: Sweet Moment Chocolates
projects.tagline: Custom e-commerce site for a local chocolatier
projects.summary: A fully custom online store for Sweet Moment, a handcrafted-chocolate business: product catalog, cart and Stripe checkout, plus an admin panel the owner uses to customize the whole site. I directed the AI coding agents that built it, tested and debugged it, and shipped it at sweetmomentchocolate.com.
description: Sweet Moment needed a storefront that looked as premium as the product. I defined what the business needed — the catalog, cart, checkout and a CMS with full customization — and drove AI coding agents through building it: a React front end, an Express API, PostgreSQL through Drizzle ORM and Stripe checkout.

A server running all year cost money the business didn't need to spend, so I added a static export to the admin: it captures the current state of the store and generates a static copy that runs free on GitHub Pages, as a backup and as an off-season version of the site.

media.alt: Sweet Moment Chocolates home page with hero, featured products, and navigation

process: My part: requirements, product direction, testing and debugging. Implementation by AI coding agents under my direction.
Shipped the full-stack store first, then added the static export to cut hosting costs.

projects.title: MyRoom
projects.tagline: A daily planner that lives on your desktop
projects.summary: MyRoom turns your desktop wallpaper into a daily planner. A hand-drawn study follows the clock from day to dusk to night, and every object in it opens something: the monitor for your day at a glance, the habit board to tick off habits, the wall calendar to count down to a trip. It ships as a Windows tray app, a new-tab browser extension and a Wallpaper Engine wallpaper, and everything stays on your own PC.
description: Seven modules — Ideas, Habits & Day Tracker, Tasks, Goals, Quotes, Schedule and Calendar — each work on their own and better together. Instead of another tab you forget to open, MyRoom is your desktop: in room mode its objects open each module as a floating panel, and in clear mode the modules sit on glass cards over your own wallpaper.

It's local-first: no account and no cloud. A small companion server bundled with the Windows app lets the app, the extension and the Wallpaper Engine build share one dataset, and one PC can share its room with others on the same network, syncing field by field and catching up after going offline.
Built by directing AI coding agents: about 43,000 lines of TypeScript and Rust, 438 automated tests, and 14 releases since July 2026.

media.alt: MyRoom's illustrated study at night: a desk with a monitor and lamp, a wall calendar, a cork board and a quote card, each one opening a module

process: Modular by rule: every read and write goes view → hook → service → repository → storage, and modules never import each other.
Accessible: AA-contrast text, a shared focus ring and full keyboard shortcuts (press ? to list them).

projects.title: MyKitchen
projects.tagline: Recipe manager on the web, as a PWA, and on Android and iOS
projects.summary: A recipe manager I built because I needed one: recipe cards with a step-by-step cook mode, a meal planner, a shopping list that knows what is missing, a list of favorite restaurants, and family links and vote sessions so a household can share recipes and decide on dinner together. It runs as a PWA and as Android and iOS apps through Capacitor.
description: MyKitchen started as a place to keep my own recipes and grew into a small product: cook mode for following a recipe at the stove, swipe mode for picking dinner, a weekly meal planner and a shopping list.

Sharing is the part I am proudest of: a family link opens a shared collection, and a vote session lets everyone pick what to cook. The backend is Cloudflare Pages Functions over a D1 database, and the same code builds the Android and iOS apps (built, not yet published to the stores). Developed by directing AI coding agents.
process: Native builds are generated from the web app, so features land everywhere at once.

projects.title: PrayerLock
projects.tagline: Native Android app that protects prayer times
projects.summary: A native Android app that manages my day around prayer: it schedules each prayer and enforces that time, so the phone cannot pull me into a distraction when it is time to pray.
description: I built it for my own day: keeping prayer times from getting lost to distraction. Like my other software, I specified it and directed AI coding agents through building and debugging it.

projects.title: AstroPortfolio
projects.summary: This portfolio is a single continuous 3D scene: a home planet with a menu, a rocket cockpit for personal information, a launch sequence, and an orbital map where every planet is a project. I designed it and directed the AI coding agents that built it, plus a static admin studio that edits the data file behind it all.
description: Everything is one scene graph and one world scale. Transitions are camera timelines rather than page loads, so the cockpit, the launch, and the solar system feel like places rather than pages.

Content lives in a single validated JSON file. Planets, labels, the cockpit screens, and the resume all read from it, and a static /admin studio edits and exports it — no backend, deployable on GitHub Pages.

media.alt: The portfolio's home planet: an astronaut on rocky terrain, the rocket on its pad, and the star behind the navigation
The orbital map: project planets on thin orbit rings around the central star

process: Built to a written art-direction contract and reviewed against screenshots of every view, on desktop and phone.

projects.title: VEX Robotics
projects.tagline: Robot concepts in Tinkercad, and the robot we built
projects.summary: In my high school robotics program I designed three robot concepts in Tinkercad (Crab Bot, Scorpion and Spin Bot) using real VEX parts and fittings, then built the team's final robot from the parts we had: it drives in four directions and has an arm with 360° of motion.
description: Each concept took a different approach to moving and manipulating: a wide, stable crab-style chassis, a scorpion with an articulated tail, and a compact spinning bot. Modelling them from real parts meant every fitting had to line up before anything was assembled.
I was the team's designer and builder; teammates handled programming and driving.

projects.title: Minecraft Adhan Clock
projects.tagline: Concept: a Raspberry Pi prayer clock styled after Minecraft
projects.summary: A design for a Raspberry Pi touchscreen clock that mimics Minecraft's day/night clock while showing Islamic prayer times. Planned, not built yet.
description: The idea is a clock you would actually want on a shelf: the familiar Minecraft clock animation driven by the real sun, with prayer times, moon phases from the Islamic calendar and adhan playback layered on top, working offline.
